verdict.rationale: Fastmail's developer page documents first-party JMAP access to mailboxes, and JMAP is an open, royalty-free IETF standard. A community user confirms SMTP access with a scoped app password. IMAP access is only glancingly implied by a migration comment, and no evidence covers standards-based mail export. missing for 10: first-party documentation of IMAP client access, first-party SMTP submission docs, standards-based export (e.g. mbox/EML), independent corroboration of protocol access.

support.subject: As a switcher, my mail stays reachable over open protocols and standard formats — IMAP/JMAP/SMTP access and standards-based export — so no client can lock me in

citations.quote: The JMAP session resource can be found at https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session
JMAP is an open standard any organisation can implement, not more proprietary lock-in from big tech companies.
Uses Fastmail SMTP for transactional emails with an app password that can only access SMTP.
